speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) in the last six months, how many local nursing homes have not been able to maintain the required ratio of care staff to residents for (i) Category I (ii) Category II (iii) Category III and (iv) Category IV residents respectively; and (b) what are the Ministry’s plans to assist the nursing homes to meet the level of staffing and level of professional skills required.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: The Lien Foundation's long-term care manpower study found that the compensation of local nurses, local nursing aides and healthcare assistants in the long-term care sector, is low compared to their counterparts in hospitals.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If the Member would like to file a specific question on that, for oral or written answer, I would be happy to provide the data.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I just have a very short supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The waiting list for nursing homes is long, as I understand it.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are there plans to incentivise care staff from the acute hospitals to perhaps try a stint in the nursing homes to help beef up the manpower there?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The skill sets for the acute hospitals and the long-term care sector, while there is significant overlap, are not exactly the same.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And we should not see the pool of manpower as completely fungible between the two.
